cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Did the boss calling us office furniture hurt you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? Are you making a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It's still in drafts. How did you feel?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Invisible. I've worked here twelve years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. Mine says 'unprofessional'; I'm changing that to 'I went home and cried.'

mechanism: A controls a complaint process to extract a colleague's hurt before admitting the same hurt.
confusable: Unlike ordinary grievance collection, A delays personal disclosure and treats requests as permissions under A's authority.
comparison: Workplace written complaint and control of access differ from family emotional discussion.
seedUse: Borrow the office-furniture insult and drafted complaint; use S01 permission handling to govern the disclosure sequence.
